source.title: Multivariate quantum signal processing with optimal query complexity
source.authors: Mingrui Jing; Xin Wang; Zhan Yu; Lei Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to be the full paper, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extracting its findings on the claim.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training and gradient results for a parameterized quantum circuit. These refine the claim’s scope: its readout-gradient variance bounds do not establish zero training error, and zero training loss is conditional on an additional Jacobian condition; an example also obstructs unconditional fitting.
record.gate_note: The study does not test CIFAR benchmarks, classical convolutional networks, or the initialization, depth, width, normalization, or learning-rate comparisons in the claim versions. It does report results about training loss for its own quantum circuit, including conditional convergence and an explicit obstruction to unconditional fitting.
record.test_reason: The study proves gradient-variance and conditional optimization results for a parameterized quantum circuit. None tests or uses the findings about classical networks specified in V1–V6. Its positive loss floor does not challenge V1, which concerns convolutional networks on CIFAR.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' optimization conclusions: the step-size bound guarantees loss decrease and vanishing gradient norm; zero training loss requires an additional Jacobian condition not established by initialization variance; and the chosen readout cannot fit some tasks. This summarizes the training analysis rather than the paper's main contribution, which is query-optimal multivariate quantum polynomial transformation.
record.recipe_differences: A parameterized quantum circuit with fixed preparation, trainable rotation angles, commuting-unitary inputs, and exact local Z readout; it is not gradient training of classical benchmark networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The initialization-variance results require query depth LN ≥ 2 and depend on branch weights and depth. The supervised loss-gradient lower bound depends on the mean target and its correlation with the first spectral moment of the last input. Zero training loss additionally depends on a uniform full-row-rank sample-Jacobian condition; the authors show this condition cannot hold when m > 2LN+1.

fits_no_version.finding: Active local-readout gradients have a uniform initialization variance lower bound; supervised loss-gradient bounds additionally depend on targets and input spectral moments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this fixed-preparation quantum circuit, initialization coordinate-gradient variance has explicit lower bounds under stated branch-weight, depth and target conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact gradient descent approaches stationarity; zero loss follows under an additional trajectory-wide Jacobian condition, while some tasks have loss at least 1/2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this quantum circuit's local readout, positive initialization gradient variance and descent to stationarity do not guarantee training fit.

record.problems: The evidence concerns a theoretical quantum learning circuit rather than the classical networks and benchmarks named in the versions. The main convergence-to-zero-loss claim is conditional; the paper notes the required Jacobian condition is not established by its variance results and is impossible when m > 2LN+1. No experimental benchmark measurements or uncertainty estimates are reported for these training claims.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported values bear on training error for the listed classical-network versions. Initialization variance results for special cases and bounds are summarized in R1–R2 rather than split into separate rows because they are theorem bounds, not separately measured model-condition outcomes.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training error on CIFAR, label corruption, model size, optimizers, early stopping and regularization.
All parts: ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima and additional student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks and normalization-free residual training.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, training speed and trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and orthogonal convolution kernels.
All parts: recovery above initial stability limits, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical rows are valid standalone findings, but their states cannot be interpreted as effects on V1–V6. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Classical convolutional networks; SGD or Adam from random initialization; CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model size and early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons in plain versus residual classical convolutional networks, shortcuts, and normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rise and curvature drop, sharpness, and divergence in classical network training.
Batch normalization comparisons, training-speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual-network results.

rows.operation_detail: Initialization variance of each active local Z readout gradient coordinate

conditions.value: exact unconditional expectation of Z on BN
fixed commuting tuple U and fixed density matrix ρS

rows.value: At least |aµ|4/(64√(2LN)) for each active coordinate in the stated ranges
rows.note: The bound is stated to hold uniformly over data dimension, query spectrum, and density matrix; it is an initialization-gradient result, not a training-error result.
rows.check: The variance bound is correctly recorded, but initialization readout-gradient variance in a quantum circuit cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: The learning model above (fixed-preparation multivariate quantum circuit)
rows.size_stated: Empirical dataset size m ≥ 1; query depth LN ≥ 2
rows.stage_stated: supervised squared-loss training; angles initialized independently and uniformly on [0, 2π)
rows.operation_detail: Initialization variance of a supervised squared-loss gradient coordinate

conditions.value: fixed dataset; same PREP, ρS and trainable angles for every sample

rows.value: At least |aµ|4/[64√(2(LN+1))] times [(mean target)² + 2(mean target-weighted first spectral moment of UN)²]
rows.note: The paper says the bound may give no positive lower bound if both displayed target quantities vanish, though other variance contributions may remain.
rows.check: This quantum loss-gradient variance bound bears on no version. In its value, the target-weighted spectral moment requires squared complex modulus, not an ordinary square. A potentially zero lower bound does not establish a partial effect.

rows.subject: The learning model above (fixed-preparation multivariate quantum circuit)
rows.stage_stated: exact gradient descent with uniform initialization
rows.operation_detail: Conditional convergence of training loss when the sample Jacobian has a uniform full-row-rank lower bound along the trajectory
rows.note: The paper says the Jacobian condition is additional and is not implied by the initialization variance bounds; it cannot hold when m > 2LN+1.
rows.check: Conditional zero-loss convergence for this quantum circuit bears on no version. Uniform initialization is unnecessary: Corollary 16 applies to Proposition 15's iterates from any starting angles satisfying the trajectory condition. Within those assumptions, convergence is fully proved rather than partial.
